units.title: Unit 1: Foundations of English Sentence Structure & Present Tenses
units.objective: Identify basic sentence patterns, choose present forms of be, form Present Simple statements and questions, and distinguish current activities from states.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: Basic English Sentence Structure (SV / SVO / SVC)
lessons.explanation_en: A common pattern in a basic affirmative English clause is Subject–Verb–Object when the verb takes an object. Other complete patterns include Subject–Verb (The train arrived.) and Subject–Verb–Complement (The report is ready.). The subject is what the clause is about; it is not always an agent performing an action. A simple subject is the head noun or pronoun; a complete subject includes its modifiers.
lessons.clarification_ar: الجملة الإنجليزية الكاملة لا تحتاج دائمًا إلى مفعول به: قد تكون فاعلًا وفعلًا فقط، أو فاعلًا وفعلًا ومفعولًا، أو فاعلًا وفعل ربط ومكمّل. الفاعل البسيط هو الاسم الأساسي أو الضمير، والفاعل الكامل يشمل الكلمات التي تصفه.
lessons.form: S + V | S + V + O | S + be/linking verb + complement
examples: The train arrived.
The student reads the textbook.
The report is ready.
common_mistakes: Omitting a required subject: use It is important to study, rather than Is important to study, in this ordinary declarative sentence.
Assuming every verb needs an object: The train arrived is already complete.
Use ordinary subject-first order when practising the basic pattern. Object fronting can be grammatical in a suitable context; The book I read must not be labelled universally ungrammatical.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.2: The Verb 'To Be' in Present Simple
lessons.explanation_en: The verb 'to be' connects a subject to a noun, adjective, or location. It changes form according to the subject: 'I am', 'he/she/it is', and 'we/you/they are'.
lessons.clarification_ar: فعل الكينونة (to be) يُستخدم للتعريف بالحالة أو المهنة أو الصفة أو المكان. يتغير شكله بحسب الفاعل: am مع الضمير I، و is مع المفرد الغائب، و are مع الجمع والضمير you.
lessons.form: Affirmative: Subject + am/is/are | Negative: Subject + am/is/are + not | Question: Am/Is/Are + Subject...?
examples: I am a project supervisor.
The report is not ready yet.
Are you available for the presentation?
common_mistakes: Confusing 'is' and 'are' with plural or compound subjects (e.g., *The results is clear* instead of *The results are clear*).
Dropping the verb 'be' altogether in nominal predicate sentences (e.g., *He teacher* instead of *He is a teacher*).

lessons.title: Lesson 1.3: Present Simple Tense and Subject-Verb Agreement
lessons.explanation_en: The Present Simple describes habitual actions, general truths, and permanent situations. When the subject is third-person singular (he, she, it, or a singular noun), add '-s' or '-es' to the base verb.
lessons.clarification_ar: يُستخدم المضارع البسيط للتعبير عن العادات والحقائق والحالات المستقرة. يضاف s أو es مع المفرد الغائب، ويتغير y إلى ies بعد حرف ساكن في مثل study → studies. يُستخدم do أو does في النفي وتكوين الأسئلة مع الأفعال الأساسية، ويعود الفعل بعدها إلى المصدر دون s.
lessons.form: Affirmative: S + Base Verb (-s/-es for he/she/it) | Negative: S + do not/does not + Base Verb | Question: Do/Does + S + Base Verb...?
examples: Dr. Miller conducts research every semester.
They do not work on weekends.
Does the course start at nine o'clock?
common_mistakes: Adding '-s' to the verb after 'does' or 'doesn't' (e.g., *He doesn't likes coffee* instead of *He doesn't like coffee*).
Forgetting the '-s' suffix for third-person singular subjects (e.g., *She work in London* instead of *She works in London*).

lessons.title: Lesson 1.4: Present Continuous Tense & State vs. Action Verbs
lessons.explanation_en: Use the Present Continuous for an activity happening now or a temporary situation around the present: am/is/are + verb-ing. Verbs such as know, own and belong normally use a simple form when they express a state. This is a meaning-based tendency, not a ban on every continuous use of every verb sometimes called stative. For example, I think this plan is useful expresses an opinion; I am thinking about the plan describes an activity.
lessons.clarification_ar: يتكوّن المضارع المستمر من am/is/are مع فعل ينتهي بـ ing، ويُستخدم للنشاط الحالي أو الوضع المؤقت. أفعال مثل know وown وbelong تستخدم عادةً زمنًا بسيطًا عندما تعبّر عن حالة. بعض الأفعال يتغير استخدامها إذا تغيّر المعنى، مثل think للرأي مقابل التفكير كنشاط.
lessons.form: Affirmative: S + am/is/are + Verb-ing | Negative: S + am/is/are + not + Verb-ing | Question: Am/Is/Are + S + Verb-ing...?
examples: The researcher is checking the data now.
I am staying in London for three months.
I understand the rule.
I think this plan is useful. / I am thinking about the plan.
common_mistakes: Using stative verbs in progressive tenses (e.g., *I am knowing the answer* instead of *I know the answer*).
Omitting the auxiliary verb 'be' (e.g., *They studying in the library* instead of *They are studying in the library*).

units.title: Unit 4: Nouns: Singular, Plural and Countability
units.objective: Form common plurals and distinguish countable and uncountable meanings in everyday adult communication.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.1: Regular and Irregular Plurals
lessons.explanation_en: Plural count nouns usually refer to more than one item. Most add -s. Many nouns ending in s, sh, ch, x or z add -es; nouns ending in consonant + y usually change y to -ies. Spellings have exceptions: check unfamiliar words. Learn irregular plurals individually: woman/women, child/children, analysis/analyses, crisis/crises, criterion/criteria. Some nouns, such as sheep and series, have the same singular and plural form. Scissors and trousers normally take plural agreement; a pair of scissors refers to one complete item, and two pairs refers to two items.
lessons.clarification_ar: الجمع يدل عادةً على أكثر من عنصر. نضيف غالبًا s أو es، ونحوّل y إلى ies بعد حرف ساكن. احفظ الجمع الشاذ مثل woman/women وcriterion/criteria؛ ولا تعمم قاعدة واحدة على كل الكلمات. نقول a pair of scissors لأداة مقص كاملة وtwo pairs لأداتين.
lessons.form: Most nouns: +s | Many s/sh/ch/x/z endings: +es | Consonant+y: -ies | Irregular examples: woman/women; criterion/criteria | a pair of scissors
examples: The supervisors reviewed several reports.
The analysts compared two analyses.
A pair of scissors is in the drawer.
common_mistakes: Use children and women, not childrens and womens, for ordinary plurals.
For one complete cutting tool, use a pair of scissors rather than a scissors.
Criterion has the plural criteria; do not add -s to criteria.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.2: Countable and Uncountable Nouns
lessons.explanation_en: Countable uses refer to separate items and allow singular and plural forms: a report, two reports. In their ordinary mass meanings, advice, information, equipment, furniture and progress are uncountable, take singular agreement and do not combine directly with a/an or a number. Use a piece of advice, three pieces of equipment or three reams of paper to specify amounts. Many and a few go with plural count nouns; much and a little go with uncountable nouns. Some and a lot of can go with either. Much is common in negatives and questions; a lot of is usually more natural in ordinary affirmative statements. Countability can change with meaning: paper as material, a paper as an article; water as a substance, a water as a serving in a suitable ordering context.
lessons.clarification_ar: الأسماء المعدودة لها مفرد وجمع. في معانيها المعتادة لا نجمع advice وinformation وequipment ولا نضع قبلها a/an مباشرة. نقول a piece of advice أوthree pieces of equipment. نستخدم many مع الجمع المعدود وmuch مع غير المعدود، وغالبًا a lot of في الإثبات العادي. قد يتغير العدّ بتغير المعنى؛ a water قد تعني حصة ماء عند الطلب.
lessons.form: Countable: a report / two reports | Uncountable: information is useful | Amounts: a piece of advice / three pieces of equipment | many reports / much information
examples: The consultant provided useful advice.
We ordered three pieces of equipment.
There was not much progress yesterday.
We received a lot of information about the project.
common_mistakes: Use information and equipment without a plural -s in their ordinary mass meanings.
Use advice or a piece of advice, not an advice.
Do not assume that a noun has the same countability in every meaning.

units.title: Unit 5: Articles: A, An, The and No Article
units.objective: Choose articles by sound and distinguish general from identifiable reference in clear contexts.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.1: A or An — Follow the Sound
lessons.explanation_en: Use a or an with a singular count noun when introducing an unspecified example. Choose by the initial sound of the following spoken word, including any adjective: a university and a European company start with /j/, while an hour and an honest answer start with a vowel sound because h is silent. MBA starts with the spoken letter name M, /em/, so use an MBA. Letter names can vary between speakers; a question about H should specify its pronunciation. A/an does not directly modify a plural noun or a noun used in an uncountable meaning. A serving meaning, such as a water in an order, is a different countable use.
lessons.clarification_ar: نختار a أوan حسب أول صوت في الكلمة التالية، بما فيها الصفة، وليس حسب أول حرف مكتوب. نقول a university وa European company لأن الصوت الأول /j/، وan hour وan honest answer لأن h صامت. لا نضعهما قبل جمع أو معنى غير معدود؛ أما الحصة مثل a water في طلب مشروب فهي استعمال معدود مختلف.
lessons.form: a + consonant sound: a university / a European company | an + vowel sound: an hour / an honest answer / an MBA
examples: He earned an MBA at a European university.
We waited for an hour before the interview.
She works as an architect.
common_mistakes: Choose by sound: an hour and a university.
Use a/an with a singular countable meaning; servings can make an otherwise mass noun countable.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.2: The or No Article — General and Specific Reference
lessons.explanation_en: Use the when the intended referent is identifiable in context, for example because it was mentioned before or both people know which item is meant. Plural count nouns and uncountable nouns often take no article when used generally: Engineers solve problems; water is essential. Compare water in general with the water in this pitcher, when referring to all the identifiable water there. A following phrase does not automatically require the: Engineers who design bridges need training can still describe a group generally. Languages and subjects normally take no article in ordinary uses. Proper names and other patterns have exceptions beyond this lesson. The symbol Ø marks an omitted article in exercises; it is not a word to insert in ordinary writing.
lessons.clarification_ar: نستخدم the عندما يكون المقصود محددًا ويمكن معرفته من السياق. عند التعميم نترك الأداة مع الجمع المعدود وغير المعدود: Engineers solve problems وWater is essential. هذا هو Zero Article ورمزه Ø في التمارين فقط. وجود وصف بعد الاسم لا يفرض the تلقائيًا؛ المهم هل المرجع محدد أم عام.
lessons.form: the + identifiable noun | No article + generic plural or uncountable noun | Ø is an exercise symbol, not a written word
examples: Water is essential for health. The water in this pitcher is filtered.
The engineers who designed our prototype are here for the meeting.
Engineers who design bridges need specialist training.
She studies economics and speaks French.
common_mistakes: For the general concept, write Life is beautiful, without the.
Do not treat every modifying phrase as proof that the is required.
Do not insert the symbol Ø into normal sentences.

units.title: Unit 6: Subject, Object and Reflexive Pronouns
units.objective: Choose ordinary formal pronoun case and distinguish reflexive, emphatic and by-pronoun patterns.

lessons.title: Lesson 6.1: Subject and Object Pronouns
lessons.explanation_en: Subject pronouns are I, you, he, she, it, we and they. Object pronouns are me, you, him, her, it, us and them. In ordinary formal written English, use a subject form as a clause subject and an object form as a verb object or after a preposition. In a coordinated phrase, temporarily remove the other person to check the case: The director invited John and me becomes The director invited me. Compare He and I wrote the report with The director spoke to him and me. Subject does not always mean an agent doing an action, and an object does not always receive a physical action.
lessons.clarification_ar: ضمائر الفاعل I وyou وhe وshe وit وwe وthey، وضمائر المفعول me وyou وhim وher وit وus وthem. في الكتابة الرسمية المعتادة نستخدم صيغة المفعول بعد حرف الجر أو كمفعول للفعل. عند العطف احذف الاسم الآخر مؤقتًا للاختبار: invited John and me تصبح invited me. موقع الفاعل لا يعني دائمًا أنه الشخص الذي ينفذ الفعل.
lessons.form: Subject: He and I wrote the report. | Verb object: invited him and me | After a preposition: with him / between you and me
examples: She presented the results to us.
The manager invited Mr. Davis and me to the meeting.
He and I wrote the report.
Between you and me, the plan needs more work.
common_mistakes: For the formal object construction, write invited John and me rather than invited John and I.
For a formal clause subject, use He and I wrote the report. Other case patterns occur in informal speech.

lessons.title: Lesson 6.2: Reflexive Pronouns
lessons.explanation_en: Reflexive forms are myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves and themselves. Yourself addresses one person; yourselves addresses more than one. A reflexive can refer back to the subject: The system updates itself. An intensive use adds emphasis: The CEO herself signed the contract; the CEO signed it herself. By ourselves can mean without other people or without outside help, depending on context. In the ordinary object construction Please contact John or me, me is the straightforward formal choice; myself is not a general replacement for me. Reflexive usage has additional patterns and dialect differences beyond this lesson.
lessons.clarification_ar: الضمائر المنعكسة تشمل yourself للمخاطب المفرد وyourselves للجمع، إلى جانب myself وhimself وherself وitself وourselves وthemselves. تعود على الفاعل أو تؤكد عليه. by ourselves قد تعني بمفردنا أو دون مساعدة خارجية بحسب السياق. في Please contact John or me نختار me كضمير مفعول عادي ولا نستبدله تلقائيًا بـmyself.
lessons.form: Reflexive: The system updates itself. | Emphasis: The CEO herself signed it. | Alone / without outside help: by ourselves
examples: The system updates itself overnight.
The engineers completed the audit by themselves.
The CEO herself signed the contract.
Please introduce yourself to the group.
common_mistakes: Use themselves as the standard plural form in these formal exercises; theirselves is a dialectal form, not the target here.
Do not assume every object referring to a person requires a reflexive. Compare She helped him with She helped herself.

units.title: Unit 7: Possessive Determiners, Pronouns and Apostrophes
units.objective: Distinguish possessive forms, contractions and singular/plural owner apostrophes.

lessons.title: Lesson 7.1: Possessive Adjectives and Pronouns
lessons.explanation_en: Possessive determiners, often called possessive adjectives, are my, your, his, her, its, our and their. They introduce a noun phrase: my book, my new book. Independent possessive pronouns include mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs: This book is mine. His has the same form in both patterns. Possessive its has no apostrophe. It's contracts it is or it has, as in It's ready and It's been checked. An independent possessive can replace a noun phrase, but the context must make the referent clear.
lessons.clarification_ar: صفات أو محددات الملكية مثل my وour وits تأتي ضمن تركيب اسمي: my book أوmy new book. ضمائر الملكية المستقلة مثل mine وours وtheirs تستبدل تركيبًا اسميًا دون اسم بعدها في هذا الاستعمال. its للملكية دون فاصلة عليا، أما it's فاختصار it is أوit has. السياق يحدد ما الذي يستبدله الضمير.
lessons.form: Possessive determiner + noun phrase: our new proposal | Independent pronoun: The proposal is ours. | its: possession / it's: it is or it has
examples: Our department has finished its proposal; their department has not finished theirs.
This desk is hers; mine is near the window.
It's clear that the company needs to update its website.
common_mistakes: Write its proposal for possession; use it's only when it is or it has fits.
Write my book or This book is mine, rather than mine book.

lessons.title: Lesson 7.2: Possessive Apostrophes ('s and s')
lessons.explanation_en: For an ordinary singular owner, add apostrophe-s: the manager's decision. For an irregular plural not ending in s, also add apostrophe-s: the women's committee. For a regular plural already ending in s, add an apostrophe after s: the clients' records. Ordinary plurals have no possessive apostrophe: The managers met yesterday. For a shared item, mark the final owner: Smith and Miller's joint presentation. For separate items, mark both: Smith's and Miller's separate offices. Style conventions can vary for singular names ending in s; those cases are outside these exercises.
lessons.clarification_ar: نضيف فاصلة عليا ثم s للمفرد وللجمع الشاذ الذي لا ينتهي بـs مثل manager's وwomen's. مع الجمع المنتظم المنتهي بـs نضع الفاصلة بعدها مثل clients' records. الجمع العادي دون ملكية لا يحتاج فاصلة. للشيء المشترك نعلّم الاسم الأخير، وللملكية المنفصلة نعلّم كل مالك.
lessons.form: Singular: manager's | Irregular plural: women's | Regular plural: clients' | Shared: Smith and Miller's presentation | Separate: Smith's and Miller's offices
examples: The auditor checked the two clients' records.
The women's forum meets every month.
We attended Smith and Miller's joint presentation.
The managers met yesterday.
common_mistakes: Place the apostrophe according to the number of owners, not the number of owned objects.
Do not add an apostrophe to an ordinary plural such as managers in The managers met yesterday.

units.title: Unit 8: Demonstratives and Quantifiers
units.objective: Match demonstrative number and reference, and choose quantity expressions with attention to countability and meaning.

lessons.title: Lesson 8.1: This, That, These and Those
lessons.explanation_en: This and that go with a singular count noun or an uncountable use; these and those go with plural count nouns. In a simple pointing situation, this/these usually indicate something nearer the speaker, and that/those something farther away. Context can also establish psychological distance, current discussion or earlier reference; distance is not a rigid rule for every use. This information is useful treats information as uncountable. On the phone, This is Sarah introduces the speaker. Demonstratives can introduce a noun phrase or stand independently: These files are ready; these are ready.
lessons.clarification_ar: نستخدم this وthat مع المفرد المعدود أو المعنى غير المعدود، وthese وthose مع الجمع المعدود. في الإشارة المكانية البسيطة this/these للقريب وthat/those للأبعد، لكن السياق قد يحدد قرب الموضوع أو بعده معنويًا. نقول this information لأن information غير معدود هنا. ويمكن لاسم الإشارة أن يأتي وحده أو قبل تركيب اسمي.
lessons.form: Near in a pointing context: this file / these files | Farther away: that file / those files | Uncountable: this information
examples: This report is on my desk; that report is on the shelf across the room.
These charts beside me are ready.
Please bring those files from the shelf across the room.
Hello, this is Mark speaking.
common_mistakes: Match number: these documents, not this documents.
With information in its ordinary uncountable meaning, use this or that, not these or those.
Do not decide distance from a shelf position alone; use the stated speaker context.

lessons.title: Lesson 8.2: Some and Any in Statements, Offers and Requests
lessons.explanation_en: With plural count nouns and uncountable uses, some often introduces an unspecified amount in an affirmative sentence: We have some files. Any is usual in neutral availability questions and in negatives meaning none: Do you have any files? We do not have any files. Some is common in offers and requests that anticipate a positive response: Would you like some water? Could I have some information? These are patterns, not absolute grammatical bans. Any can occur in offers or requests with a different emphasis; a coffee can mean a serving. Some can remain under a negative to refer to a particular subset: We did not receive some of the replies means some replies were missing, not necessarily all. Affirmative free-choice any, such as Choose any folder, is another use.
lessons.clarification_ar: تشيع some للكميات غير المحددة في الإثبات وفي عروض وطلبات نتوقع فيها ردًا إيجابيًا. وتشيع any في السؤال المحايد عن التوفر وفي النفي بمعنى لا شيء. هذه أنماط وليست قواعد منع مطلقة؛ يمكن استخدام any في بعض الطلبات والعروض، كما قد تأتي some مع النفي للدلالة على جزء محدد لم يتحقق. قارن لم تصل أي ردود مع لم يصل بعض الردود.
lessons.form: An unspecified amount: some files / some water | Neutral question: any files? | None: not any files | Common offer: Would you like some water?
examples: We have some spare folders.
Would you like some water?
Could you send me some details?
We did not receive any replies.
We did not receive some of the replies; the rest arrived.
common_mistakes: Do not call every offer with any ungrammatical; some and any can carry different expectations.
For no replies at all, use did not receive any replies. Some under a negative can mean only a subset was missing.

lessons.title: Lesson 8.3: Much, Many and A Lot Of
lessons.explanation_en: Much goes with uncountable uses; many goes with plural count nouns. Much is especially common in negatives and questions: not much time; how much money? Many is possible in affirmative sentences too: Many people work here. A lot of and lots of work with both types and are common in everyday affirmative sentences: a lot of files; a lot of time. Affirmative much can be grammatical, especially in formal contexts or with modifiers such as too much and so much; it is not universally wrong. Countability depends on the meaning in the sentence.
lessons.clarification_ar: نستخدم much مع غير المعدود وmany مع الجمع المعدود. تشيع much في السؤال والنفي، ويمكن استخدام many في الإثبات أيضًا. تصلح a lot of وlots of للنوعين وتشيعان في الإثبات اليومي. استخدام much في الإثبات ليس خطأ مطلقًا، خصوصًا في الأسلوب الرسمي أو مع too وso.
lessons.form: Uncountable: much time / much advice | Plural count: many files | Both: a lot of files / a lot of time
examples: We do not have much time.
How many people attended the meeting?
Many people use this office.
We received a lot of useful advice.
common_mistakes: Use many employees, not much employees.
Use much advice or a lot of advice, not many advice, for the uncountable meaning.
A lot of is often more natural than unmodified much in an ordinary affirmative sentence; this is a usage tendency.

lessons.title: Lesson 8.4: A Few, Few, A Little and Little
lessons.explanation_en: A few and few go with plural count nouns; a little and little go with uncountable uses. A few and a little introduce a small amount, often with a more positive focus on what exists. They do not guarantee that the amount is sufficient: We have a little money, but not enough for the tickets. Few and little emphasize a low amount, often less than hoped or needed; they do not necessarily mean zero. Contrast We have a few helpers with We have few helpers, and We have a little time with We have little time. Context determines whether any amount is enough.
lessons.clarification_ar: تأتي a few وfew مع الجمع المعدود، وa little وlittle مع غير المعدود. وجود a يركز غالبًا على وجود كمية قليلة، لكنه لا يضمن أنها كافية: معنا قليل من المال لكنه لا يكفي للتذاكر. دون a يكون التركيز غالبًا على القلة أو النقص، وليس بالضرورة انعدام الكمية تمامًا. يحدد السياق إن كانت الكمية كافية.
lessons.form: Plural count: a few helpers / few helpers | Uncountable: a little help / little help | A small amount does not automatically mean enough
examples: A few colleagues offered to help.
We have few volunteers, so we need more.
We have a little time, but not enough to finish.
There is little hope of finishing today.
common_mistakes: Use a little advice rather than a few advice for the ordinary uncountable meaning.
Do not equate a little with enough, or little with zero in every context.

units.title: Unit 9: Time Reference, Boundaries and Duration
units.objective: Choose time expressions by their clock/calendar reference, event sequence, deadline, continuing limit or length.

lessons.title: Lesson 9.1: At, In and On for Time
lessons.explanation_en: Use at for clock times and expressions such as at noon and at night. In goes with months, years, seasons and general parts of the day: in May, in 2026, in summer, in the morning. On goes with days and dates, including a named day plus part of that day: on Monday, on 15 May, on Monday morning. At Christmas refers to the holiday period; on Christmas Day refers to the day. At the weekend is usual in British English and on the weekend in American English. These patterns include idioms; at night is not the same pattern as in the morning. Time phrases beginning next, last, this or every commonly take no at/in/on: next Monday, this morning, every Friday. Present simple can describe a timetable: The meeting starts on Monday.
lessons.clarification_ar: نستخدم at مع الساعة وتعبيرات مثل at noon وat night، وin مع الشهور والسنوات والفصول وأجزاء اليوم العامة. نستخدم on مع اليوم أو التاريخ وكذلك on Monday morning. نقول at Christmas لفترة العطلة وon Christmas Day لليوم نفسه. at the weekend شائعة بريطانيًا وon the weekend أمريكيًا. غالبًا لا نضيف حرف جر قبل next أوlast أوthis أوevery في تعبيرات الوقت.
lessons.form: at nine / at noon / at night | in May / in 2026 / in the morning | on Monday / on Monday morning | next Monday: no preposition
examples: The board meeting starts at nine on Monday.
The calendar includes a training event in 2026.
We review the plan at the weekend. (British English)
We review the plan on the weekend. (American English)
The workshop starts next Monday.
common_mistakes: Use on Monday and at nine, rather than in Monday or in nine.
Accept both at the weekend and on the weekend in their usual varieties.
A longer phrase can change the pattern: in the morning but on Monday morning.

lessons.title: Lesson 9.2: Before and After
lessons.explanation_en: Before means earlier than the reference event; after means later. Both can be followed by a noun phrase or pronoun: before the meeting, after it. A following verb in the preposition pattern takes an -ing form: before sending the report, after checking the figures. The person understood to perform that -ing action normally matches the subject or understood subject of the main instruction: Check the figures before sending the report. Before and after can also introduce a full clause with its own subject: before you leave, after the meeting ends. Do not confuse that full-clause pattern with a bare verb directly after the preposition. The sequence must come from context, not from assuming that scheduling an event happens after an earlier task.
lessons.clarification_ar: before تعني قبل الحدث المرجعي وafter تعني بعده. يمكن أن يتبعهما اسم أوضمير أوصيغة ing: before sending the report. في هذا النمط يكون الشخص المفهوم للفعل ing عادة هو فاعل الجملة أوالمخاطب في التعليمات. يمكن أيضًا أن يتبعهما فاعل وفعل في جملة كاملة: before you leave. التوقيت الفعلي للسياق هو الذي يحدد قبل أم بعد؛ جدولة اجتماع لاحق لا تعني أن الجدولة نفسها حدثت بعده.
lessons.form: before / after + noun phrase: before the meeting | + -ing: after checking | Full clause: before you leave
examples: Please check the figures before sending the report.
We review the results after finishing the tests.
Please call me before you leave.
The team takes a break after the meeting.
common_mistakes: In the -ing pattern, write before leaving, not before leave or before to leave.
Before you leave is grammatical because you leave is a full clause.
State the intended order of events clearly when choosing before or after.

lessons.title: Lesson 9.3: From…To, Until and By
lessons.explanation_en: From…to marks a starting and ending time: from eight to five. From…until is also possible for an interval. Until, or till, describes a situation continuing up to a reference point: The office stays open until five. By expresses a deadline, at or before a time: Please send the report by Friday. A deadline does not require the action to continue through that whole period. Compare Stay here until five with Arrive here by five. Until can also introduce a clause, as in Stay until the meeting ends. By and until have other patterns, but these exercises focus on ordinary deadlines and continuing situations.
lessons.clarification_ar: تحدد from…to بداية الفترة ونهايتها، ويمكن استخدام from…until أيضًا. تشير until أوtill إلى استمرار حالة حتى وقت معين: يبقى المكتب مفتوحًا حتى الخامسة. تشير by إلى موعد أقصى، أي في ذلك الوقت أو قبله: أرسل التقرير بحلول الجمعة. قارن البقاء حتى الخامسة مع الوصول في الخامسة أو قبلها.
lessons.form: Interval: from eight to five / from eight until five | Continuing situation: open until five | Deadline: send by Friday
examples: The office is open from eight to five.
The assistants stay at the desk until five.
Please send the report by Friday afternoon.
Please stay until the meeting ends.
common_mistakes: For an ordinary one-time submission deadline, use send the report by Friday.
For staying continuously up to five, use stay until five.
A deadline expressed with by includes the reference time, unless context states a stricter cutoff.

lessons.title: Lesson 9.4: During, While and For
lessons.explanation_en: During is followed by a noun phrase and locates something within a period or event: during the meeting. It does not by itself specify how long the action lasts or guarantee that it lasts through the whole event. While commonly introduces a clause with a subject and verb: while she writes the report. In a reduced clause, while can also precede an -ing form: while checking the figures. For with a length of time answers how long: for two hours. In the intended ordinary duration use, choose for six months rather than during six months. Other during phrases can identify a period, such as during the next six months; these must not be treated as universally impossible. Since and perfect tenses are deferred to later lessons.
lessons.clarification_ar: تتبع during بتركيب اسمي لتحديد الفترة التي يقع فيها الحدث، دون أن تعني بالضرورة استمراره طوال الفترة. تتبع while غالبًا بفاعل وفعل، ويمكن أن تأتي بعدها صيغة ing في جملة مختصرة. تستخدم for مع طول المدة مثل for two hours. تعبير during the next six months ممكن لتحديد فترة؛ لذلك لا نعمم منع during مع كل تعبير يحتوي على رقم. نؤجل since والأزمنة التامة لدروسها.
lessons.form: When within an event: during + noun phrase | Simultaneous clause: while + subject + verb | How long: for + length of time
examples: Please keep your phone silent during the presentation.
She writes the report while her colleague checks the figures.
The team meets for two hours every Tuesday.
Please take notes while checking the figures.
common_mistakes: For a specified length, write work for six months. For an identified period, during the next six months can be appropriate.
Use while she works, not during she works, for the full-clause pattern.
Do not equate during an event with for the entire duration of that event.

units.title: Unit 10: Place and Movement
units.objective: Describe locations and routes using an explicit spatial context, accepting legitimate differences of emphasis.

lessons.title: Lesson 10.1: In, On and At for Place
lessons.explanation_en: In often describes being inside a space or within a city or country: in the office, in Paris. On often describes contact with a surface: on the desk; it also occurs in patterns such as on the second floor. At can identify a point, activity or site: at the entrance, at the office, at the conference. At the office and in the office can both be natural, with different emphasis. A package at the reception desk can be at that service point, while a package on the reception desk rests on its surface. Context matters: do not assume that each place noun always takes exactly one preposition. Street expressions also vary by variety and context.
lessons.clarification_ar: تشيع in للوجود داخل مساحة أوفي مدينة أودولة، وon لملامسة سطح ولتعبيرات مثل on the second floor. قد تشير at إلى نقطة أوموقع أونشاط. يمكن أن تصح at the office وin the office مع اختلاف التركيز. والطرد at the reception desk موجود عند نقطة الاستقبال، أما on the reception desk فيستقر على سطح المكتب. السياق هو الذي يحدد المعنى؛ لا نفرض حرف جر واحدًا لكل اسم مكان.
lessons.form: Inside: in the office | City: in Paris | Surface: on the desk | Site or point: at the entrance / at the office
examples: The manager is working at her desk in the office.
The reports are on the table.
The package is at the reception desk. It is resting on the desk.
The CEO lives in Paris.
common_mistakes: For ordinary residence in a city, write lives in Paris.
At the office and in the office can both be correct; state the intended meaning.
Do not treat a surface and a functional service point as the same spatial description.

lessons.title: Lesson 10.2: Under, Behind, Next To and Between
lessons.explanation_en: Under places something below another object; behind places it at the back relative to the stated viewpoint. Next to means adjacent to, and beside is often similar. Between can describe a position with distinct things on different sides; it does not require an exact midpoint. Although basic examples often use two objects, between is not restricted to exactly two participants in every use. A diagram or explicit arrangement is needed to determine spatial relationships: the noun names alone do not tell you where a printer stands.
lessons.clarification_ar: تشير under إلى موضع أسفل شيء، وbehind إلى ما يقع خلفه من وجهة النظر المحددة. تعني next to المجاورة. قد تصف between موضعًا تحيط به أشياء مميزة من جهات مختلفة ولا تشترط المنتصف الدقيق. وهي ليست مقصورة دائمًا على شيئين في كل استعمال. نحتاج ترتيبًا مكانيًا واضحًا لاختيار الإجابة، وليس مجرد أسماء الأثاث.
lessons.form: Below: under the desk | At the back: behind reception | Adjacent: next to John | Distinct flanking objects: between the cabinet and the shelf
examples: The spare cables are under the desk.
The archive room is behind reception.
Sarah sits next to John.
In the row cabinet – printer – bookshelf, the printer is between the other two items.
common_mistakes: Use next to in this ordinary adjacency pattern, not next alone.
Do not claim that between is always wrong with more than two participants.
Check the stated viewpoint and layout before choosing a position word.

lessons.title: Lesson 10.3: To, Into and Out Of
lessons.explanation_en: To marks a destination in patterns such as go to the office. Into explicitly describes movement from outside to inside: walk into the room. Out of describes movement from inside to outside: take the laptop out of the bag. In can also occur naturally with movement verbs in some constructions, such as put it in the box or step in. Into is useful when the task specifically asks for explicit entry; do not label every dynamic in construction an error. Out from also has legitimate uses in other patterns, so it is not universally forbidden.
lessons.clarification_ar: تحدد to الوجهة في تراكيب مثل go to the office. وتوضح into الانتقال من الخارج إلى الداخل، بينما توضح out of الانتقال من الداخل إلى الخارج. يمكن أن تصح in مع بعض أفعال الحركة مثل put it in the box أوstep in؛ لذلك لا نصف كل استعمال حركي لها بالخطأ. نختار into عندما نريد إبراز الدخول صراحة.
lessons.form: Destination: go to the office | Explicit entry: walk into the room | Removal: take the laptop out of the bag
examples: The manager walks into the building and goes to the meeting room.
On work trips, we drive to the hotel and stay in our room.
She takes the laptop out of her bag and puts it on the desk.
Please step into the elevator.
common_mistakes: Do not equate in with a universal absence of movement.
To the building names a destination; into the building explicitly describes entry.
Read the starting and ending positions when choosing into or out of.

lessons.title: Lesson 10.4: Through, Across and Along
lessons.explanation_en: Through often focuses on passing within a space or passage, possibly entering and emerging: through a tunnel, through a gate, through a park. The space need not be fully enclosed. Across focuses on reaching the other side: across the street or across an open bridge. Along focuses on following the length or course of a path. Through and along can both describe travel in a tunnel or corridor, with different emphasis. A street can also occur with different path words depending on the route. Describe the intended route rather than assigning a single mandatory preposition to each noun.
lessons.clarification_ar: تركز through غالبًا على المرور داخل مساحة أوممر وربما الدخول من طرف والخروج من الآخر، ولا تشترط مساحة مغلقة تمامًا. وتركز across على الانتقال إلى الجانب الآخر، بينما تركز along على اتباع طول مسار. قد يصح through وalong مع النفق أوالممر بمعنيين متقاربين لكن بتركيز مختلف؛ لذا نوضح الطريق المقصود ولا نفرض حرف جر واحدًا على اسم المكان.
lessons.form: Within a passage: through the tunnel | To the other side: across the street | Following a length: along the corridor
examples: They walk across the street from one pavement to the other.
Please go through the main gate.
The guide walks along the corridor.
The officer travels through the tunnel; along the tunnel can also describe following its length.
common_mistakes: Do not call every through the street or through the bridge phrase ungrammatical without a route context.
A covered passage and an open crossing can invite different descriptions.
Along a tunnel and through a tunnel may both be valid; explain the emphasis.

units.title: Unit 11: Past Simple & Irregular Verbs
units.objective: Form and apply the past simple tense using 'was/were', regular verbs with correct -ed spelling rules, common irregular verbs, and negatives/questions using 'did/didn't' in clear past time contexts.

lessons.title: Lesson 11.1: Past Simple of Be: Was and Were
lessons.explanation_en: For the ordinary past simple of be, use was with I/he/she/it and singular noun phrases, and were with you/we/they and plural noun phrases. You takes were for one person as well as several people. Negatives are was not/wasn't and were not/weren't. Invert be and the subject for ordinary questions: Was he here? Were you busy? These basic past-be questions and negatives do not use did. Other constructions and dialect patterns are outside these drills.
lessons.clarification_ar: في الماضي البسيط المعتاد لـbe نستخدم was مع I/he/she/it والمفرد، وwere مع you/we/they والجمع. تأخذ you الصيغة were للمخاطب المفرد والجمع. نضيف not للنفي ونقدم was/were على الفاعل للسؤال. لا نستخدم did في هذا النمط الأساسي لسؤال أو نفي be.
lessons.form: Affirmative: Subject + 'was'/'were' | Negative: Subject + 'wasn't'/'weren't' | Question: 'Was'/'Were' + Subject + ...?
examples: The manager was in the office yesterday.
The clients were not happy with the schedule last week.
Were you at the meeting yesterday?
common_mistakes: Using 'did' with 'be' in questions or negatives (e.g., *Did you be at the meeting?* instead of *Were you at the meeting?*).
Confusing subject agreement (e.g., *We was busy* instead of *We were busy*).

lessons.title: Lesson 11.2: Regular Past Simple Verbs and -ed Spelling Rules
lessons.explanation_en: Regular past verbs normally add -ed: work/worked. After final e, add d: live/lived. After consonant+y, change y to i before ed: study/studied; vowel+y keeps y: play/played. In a one-syllable verb ending in one vowel letter representing a short vowel, followed by one final consonant letter, commonly double that consonant: plan/planned, stop/stopped. Do not double final w, x or y: snow/snowed, fix/fixed, play/played. Longer verbs depend on stress and sometimes spelling variety; they are not covered by a universal short-verb rule. In affirmative past-simple statements, these forms are the same for I, you, he, she, it, we and they.
lessons.clarification_ar: نضيف ed عادةً، أوd بعد e. نحول y إلى i بعد حرف ساكن: study/studied، ونحتفظ بها بعد حرف علة: play/played. في أفعال المقطع الواحد ذات حرف علة قصير واحد ثم حرف ساكن نهائي واحد، نضاعف الساكن غالبًا مثل plan/planned وstop/stopped، باستثناء w وx وy. للأفعال الأطول قواعد تعتمد على النبر وأحيانًا على تنوع الإملاء؛ لا نعمم المضاعفة على كل فعل قصير.
lessons.form: Base Verb + '-ed' / '-d' / '-ied' / doubled consonant + '-ed'
examples: The team worked late yesterday.
She planned the budget last month.
He studied the report yesterday morning.
We played a short training game last Friday.
common_mistakes: The past of plan is planned. Planed exists as the past of the different verb plane; it is not the past of plan.
Write studied, not studyed, for study; write played, not plaied, for play.
Do not double every final consonant: fix becomes fixed, not fixxed.

lessons.title: Lesson 11.3: Common Irregular Past Simple Verbs
lessons.explanation_en: Common irregular verbs do not form their ordinary past simple with -ed. Learn go/went, see/saw, have/had, make/made, take/took, write/wrote, buy/bought, come/came, give/gave, say/said and meet/met. Use the past form in an affirmative statement with a clear past context. In these standard written exercises, use I saw for the ordinary simple past, not I seen. Regular verbs such as sign/signed belong to the regular pattern instead. Leave becomes left, as in I left the table unfinished.
lessons.clarification_ar: للأفعال الشاذة صيغ ماضٍ نحتاج تعلمها، مثل go/went وhave/had وwrite/wrote وbuy/bought وmeet/met. نستخدم صيغة الماضي في الإثبات مع سياق ماضٍ واضح. في الكتابة القياسية المعتادة نقول I saw للماضي البسيط. أما sign/signed فهو فعل منتظم.
lessons.form: Subject + Irregular Past Verb (e.g., went / saw / had / made)
examples: The director went to London last week.
We bought new equipment last Tuesday.
She wrote the report and made a task list yesterday.
I left the table unfinished yesterday.
common_mistakes: Use went and bought for the ordinary past of go and buy, rather than adding -ed.
In these standard written past-simple exercises, use I saw rather than I seen.

lessons.title: Lesson 11.4: Negatives and Questions with Did/Didn't (vs. Was/Were)
lessons.explanation_en: For ordinary past-simple negatives with lexical verbs, use did not/didn't plus the base form: I didn't go. Most yes/no and object questions use did + subject + base form: Did you meet her? Why did they change the plan? Be uses was/were directly in the basic past patterns: Was she present? She wasn't present. Do not put was/were after did in these patterns. Subject questions such as Who called? are a different pattern and do not normally need did; they are not assessed in this batch.
lessons.clarification_ar: في نفي الماضي البسيط مع الأفعال العادية نستخدم did not أوdidn't ثم الفعل الأساسي. وفي معظم أسئلة نعم/لا وأسئلة المفعول نستخدم did ثم الفاعل والفعل الأساسي. أما be ففي هذه الأنماط نسأل وننفي مباشرةً بـwas/were. أسئلة الفاعل مثل Who called? نمط آخر لا يحتاج عادةً إلى did وليس موضع التقييم هنا.
lessons.form: Negative: Subject + 'didn't' + Base Verb | Question: 'Did' + Subject + Base Verb ...?
examples: The engineer didn't attend the safety brief yesterday.
Did you send the contract to the legal team last night?
Why did they change the project schedule last week?
common_mistakes: Using a past tense verb after 'did' or 'didn't' (e.g., *I didn't went* instead of *I didn't go*).
Using 'did' with 'was/were' (e.g., *Did she was present?* instead of *Was she present?*).

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a concise personal introduction paragraph (50–80 words) describing your profession, daily work routines, and one project you are currently working on. You MUST include at least two sentences in the Present Simple tense and two sentences in the Present Continuous tense.
writing_tasks.model_response: I work as a designer at a small company. I usually create posters and discuss ideas with my colleagues every morning. At the moment, I am preparing a short presentation for a new client. This week, I am also learning how to explain my design choices more clearly during our meetings.
review_criteria: At least two sentences use the Present Simple appropriately for a role or routine.
At least two sentences use the Present Continuous appropriately for a current or temporary activity.
Check subject–verb agreement and required auxiliary verbs.
Aim for 50–80 words with a clear connection between sentences; word count alone does not establish writing quality.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a professional supply request memo (60–90 words) to your office administrator. Include at least two plural count nouns, two uncountable nouns with suitable partitives or quantifiers, and examples of a/an and the where appropriate.
writing_tasks.model_response:
Dear Sarah,

I am writing to request additional office supplies for our department. We need a new printer for the main office and two pairs of scissors for the design team. In addition, please order three reams of paper and a box of pens. We also require some advice regarding the delivery schedule for the new computer equipment. Thank you for your assistance with this matter.

Best regards,
Mark
review_criteria: Check ordinary plural forms, including supplies, pairs and pens.
Use suitable amounts with uncountable nouns, such as three reams of paper and some advice.
Choose a/an by sound and the for identifiable references.
Aim for 60–90 words and a clear professional request. Word count alone does not measure writing quality.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a formal email excerpt (60–90 words) reporting on a joint project. Include an ordinary compound object pronoun phrase, a by + reflexive phrase for independence, a possessive determiner before a noun, and a regular plural possessive ending in s'.
writing_tasks.model_response:
Dear Ms. Sterling,

I am pleased to report that the project team completed the financial audit ahead of schedule. The division head assigned Mr. Davis and me to review the clients' account statements. We verified all transaction records by ourselves and identified key cost-saving opportunities. Our department will present its final recommendations during tomorrow's executive briefing.

Sincerely,
David Vance
review_criteria: Check ordinary formal object case in a coordinated object, such as assigned Mr. Davis and me.
Use a by + reflexive phrase referring clearly to the people working independently.
Use possessive determiners appropriately; distinguish its from the contraction it's.
Place the apostrophe after s for regular plural owners, such as clients' statements.
Aim for 60–90 words and a clear professional message. Word count alone is not a writing-quality assessment.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a project status email (60–90 words). Include this or these for current work, some in an offer or request, much or many in a negative statement, and a few or a little for a small quantity. Use simple adult workplace language.
writing_tasks.model_response:
Dear Mr. Vance,

I am writing to update you on our current progress. This week, our team completed the preliminary market analysis. We did not encounter many difficulties during the testing phase. However, we still need a little time to finalize the technical documentation. Could you please send us some feedback on these draft slides when you are available?

Best regards,
Sarah
review_criteria: Match demonstrative number and the intended reference, such as this week or these slides.
Use some naturally in the requested offer or request; other contexts may allow any.
Match much/many with the intended uncountable/plural count meaning in the negative statement.
Use a few or a little for a small amount; do not assume this automatically means enough.
Aim for 60–90 words and a clear update. Word count alone does not measure writing quality.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a short project schedule email (60–90 words). Include a clock time with at and a day with on, a deadline with by, a continuing situation with until, and a length of time with for. You may also use during for an event. Use present-simple timetables, current situations and polite instructions; future forms and since are not required.
writing_tasks.model_response:
Dear Ms. Vance,

Here is our project schedule. The planning meeting starts on Monday at ten. We discuss the design for two hours during the morning session. The office stays open until six, so there is time to check the notes. Please send your comments by five on Friday. Before sending them, please check the dates and names in the report. Thank you for your help with this project.

Best regards,
Mark
review_criteria: Use at with the clock time and on with the named day.
Distinguish the by deadline from a situation continuing until an endpoint.
Use for to state a length, and during to identify an event if included.
Use clear timetable/current forms or instructions; advanced tenses are not needed.
Aim for 60–90 words and a clear schedule. Word count alone does not establish writing quality.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a workplace location message (60–90 words) giving a colleague directions to a meeting. Include at or in for location, next to or between for relative position, into or out of for entry/exit, and through or across for a route. Use simple present and instructions. Describe the route clearly.
writing_tasks.model_response:
Hello Mark,

Our meeting is in Room 302 at the main office. Please walk through the lobby and across the open courtyard to the west wing. Take the elevator to the third floor. Room 302 is next to the staff lounge. Step into the room when you arrive. I am waiting at the table near the window with the meeting notes.

Best regards,
Sarah
review_criteria: Use at/in to describe the intended location; more than one emphasis can be valid.
Make next to/between relationships clear from the layout.
Use into/out of for the intended explicit entry or exit.
Describe the route with through/across consistently; do not assume one mandatory preposition per noun.
Aim for 60–90 words and clear usable directions. Word count alone is not a writing-quality score.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a 60–90-word summary email about your work yesterday. Include was/were, at least two regular affirmative past verbs, at least two irregular affirmative past verbs other than was/were, and a negative sentence with didn't or did not. Do not use past continuous or perfect tenses.
writing_tasks.model_response:
Dear Mr. Davis,

Here is a summary of my work yesterday. I arrived at the office early and checked the urgent emails. I was in a team meeting for two hours. Later, I called two clients, wrote the weekly report and made a new task list. I didn't receive the revised budget, so I left that table unfinished and asked my colleague for help.

Best regards,
Alex
review_criteria: Match was/were to the intended subject; you takes were for singular and plural addressees.
Use at least two regular affirmative past verbs, such as arrived, checked or called.
Use at least two irregular affirmative past verbs other than was/were, such as wrote and made.
Use did not or didn't followed by a base verb for the negative.
Aim for 60–90 words and a clear past-time summary. Word count alone does not establish writing quality.
